text: 5.	In 1893, Chicago inventor Whitcomb Judson patented a "clasp locker" — a hook-and-eye fastening device for shoes that was complicated, prone to bursting open, and almost completely ignored by the public. Swedish-American engineer Gideon Sundback joined his company and by 1914 had developed a vastly superior design that was reliable, smooth, and could be manufactured at scale. For years the fastener was used almost exclusively in boots and tobacco pouches, and it still had no popular name. In 1923, the rubber company X adopted Sundback's fastener for a new line of galoshes and built a marketing campaign around what it called its Y galoshes — the name Y chosen to evoke the sharp sound the fastener made when pulled open quickly. The name proved catchier than the product. Within a decade Y was being used to describe the fastener itself rather than the boots, and from there it spread to clothing, luggage, bags, and virtually every other product that needed a quick, secure closure. ID X (10 points) and Y (5 points).
